Appendix F: Self-trust, outside guidance, and oracle-like states

[Please see how to use synchronicity as a cue, not an oracle, above.]

One of the issues here is that people vary dramatically in how suggestible they are, both internally and externally, and different people vary in how suggestible they are in different states. Different types of suggestion (commands, imagery, music, metaphors, spiritual, etc) can be very different for different people. So there are definite advantages to both having someone work with you (pacing, containment, another set of eyes), and doing things yourself. Being able to follow up immediately, to correct something in real time, to have a line of communication with protectors, etc.

That said, self hypnosis may be the best way of talking to your subconscious on a day to day basis. If you’re dealing with particularly complicated trauma, blind spots, dissociation, destabilisation, or relational wounds that need another nervous system, skilled outside support may be best.

Finding a hypnotist who can work with you

What they are trained in (what they can treat) How they use hypnosis What they will do if things don't "fit" (if they are treating trauma, did they have specific training on trauma and dissociation? Having hypnosis certifications matters, but doesn't mean they are trained in trauma care)

What has/hasn't worked for you in the past How direct you want them to be What kind of touch (if any) you are ok with What kind of imagery (if any) you are ok with What you want them to do if you want them to stop What they will do if things go unexpected during or after the session What they do if you aren't sure if something is a memory or not How they will do the full return (coming out of hypnosis) at the end of the session You should be able to be firmly encouraged, but not forced to continue if you don't want to.

Then afterwards, check in about what was actually done, regardless of what you might call the method. Ask the person why they did what they did, if they told you in advance. Did you agree to it? How did the person respond to you? Keep in mind that just because something made you uncomfortable, it doesn't mean it was "bad," but if they saw your discomfort as meaning that you needed more of it, that might be something to look into. You might even be able to use this app or ask around to see if someone can tell you what the things they did meant. They probably won't be able to tell you if the person was "certified" in them or not, though. Then you can decide if you want to try learning to do self-hypnosis, using both, or find someone else. Those are all good options.

When the subconscious speaks like an oracle

Your subconscious is amazing at picking up on things your conscious mind isn't getting. Whether it's anticipations, reading patterns, or just picking up on uncanny things, it's good to respect what your subconscious is picking up on. But just because your subconscious gives you an image or tells you to do something, that doesn't mean you need to treat it like an order.

Especially if it's a big thing, or something that can't be easily undone, slow it down to the scale of the thing. Look at it with your adult's eyes, and take it to council.

The council — internal first, then outward

Ask your child, your adult, your conscious mind, your subconscious mind, your intuition, your analytical mind. But if it's bigger than all of those, ask outside of yourself, too. The bigger and more un-undoable something is, the more you want to reach outside.

Ask people who love you, people who are like you, people who have done what you are thinking of doing. Sometimes it is right to go it alone, but I would suggest making it the last step, after you've tried to get council.

On the other hand, it is possible to give your power away. Seeking counsel can quietly turn into abdicating to an authority figure. Another person doesn’t get automatic trust, or automatic dismissal.

Sometimes you need the support of your peers. In Hearthwork, the concept is that you give each other equal time, warmth, confidentiality, and acceptance of “no” as an answer, and you act for each other as Nurturer and Protector, but not as Guide. Then you reverse roles. Sometimes, with a question asked carefully and at the right time, your peers can help you hear your own Guide more clearly, but they don’t interpret what you experience.

Forgiveness without bypass

There are a lot of times when we can not ‘force’ forgiveness on ourselves, it has to come from a place of understanding otherwise it can be bypassing. However, if we remain in the anger forever, we are allowing the injury to dictate how we live our lives in the present. So how do we hold all of this? We simply remember that it can all be true.

It can all be true that:

A helpful understanding to come to, is that while their actions were harmful, in a sense, they could only make the moves they made, given their accumulated nature at the time (conditioning, history, pain, capacity, etc). This doesn’t negate that harm was caused, holding someone accountable, allowing for consequences, working on making different moves now, etc. It simply helps us come to a place where we aren’t expecting something from someone that they can’t give. It doesn’t make their limitations matter any less.

“You don’t have to forgive before you’re ready. I won’t use spirituality to silence your pain. And I won’t build our whole life around this wound forever.”

Some questions that may be helpful to ask when coming to a place of forgiveness, while still holding all of the above:

What actually happened? What was the impact? What boundaries need to be set? What shaped the other person(s) into someone capable of that harm? What is theirs? What is mine? What does accountability require? How can I let this go, without denying any of the above?

For self-forgiveness, name what you did, without taking responsibility for what wasn't yours. Let the remorse register the harm, or how it went against your values, without making yourself a permanent criminal.

Take responsibility, feel the remorse, then rectify if you can, and then let it go. Be specific about the action you took, and the impact it had, feel the remorse, do what you can to rectify or keep it from happening again, and then stop holding yourself hostage.

Hypnotism can happen in a therapist’s office, but it can also happen through music, marketing, religious rituals, sexual chemistry, charismatic authority, social media, grief, fear, political messaging, sense of belonging, fatigue, love, trauma, beauty, etc.

Even when not actively engaging the conscious mind, there are many ways to influence people. Marketers and interface designers know this perfectly well. In the Federal Trade Commission’s report on “dark patterns,” they describe designs that trick or manipulate consumers. The Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) describes commercial patterns that steer, deceive, coerce, or manipulate people toward choices that may work against their interests.

Conscious agreement, unconscious receptivity, emotional compliance, legal and ethical consent. Can people have their minds influenced without conscious agreement of their adult self?

Induction: gathering attention without disappearing

Hypnotic inductions are intended to bring your attention together so that you can hear some material that you might not hear when you are sober. It is not intended as a place where you surrender yourself, or go to sleep, or need to obey anyone. Sometimes if you are sober and finding it hard to focus because you are distracted or too analytical or putting up with resistance to working on something, an induction can be useful. However if you are already pretty trancey (because you have meditated before hand, or because you are drunk on loveyhuasca or doing lucid dreaming or working on grief or listening to music or praying or tired or whatever) you might want to skip to orienting yourself and making sure you are contained before you go any further.

If you do want to induce a trance make it as deep as you need it to be for you to be able to be focussed, warm, receptive, embodied and able to stop when you need to. It doesn't have to be very deep at all.

What an induction is actually doing

It's preparation, gathering up your attention, sometimes it's deepening too. It will work better if you make it fit to what comes up for you. Counting is one way of gathering up your attention. You can also do it through talking, or telling a story, or movement, or sound, or encouraging you to be curious about something. If you do it through any of these means, say so. Just because it's done elegantly, doesn't mean it has to be covert.

It may be a good idea to try out the suggestion you are going to make on a simple target, to see if it works for you, before you go to the trouble of deepening. If you have already got what you want, you can always develop a more receptive response to it afterwards, you don't need all the ceremony to make it happen.

Please don’t put six metaphors in one trance

Decide what you are going to do, and how you are going to anchor it at the beginning, and how you are going to get back. Do you want it to be warm or firm or directed or neutral or what? Don't use floating and going down stairs and going through gardens and going to inner places and seeing a colour and talking to a child inside, even if they all appeal to you! If you need to change metaphors, do it consciously.

It is OK to do this with no imagery, you will get the signal some other way. Try and make the language you use for counting in etc match the world you have chosen. Come back out again by reversing the journey in some way. It is ok to borrow qualities, but don't be somebody else.

Try and restrict yourself to one key verb, or a particular sense quality, or a small bit of text you repeat to yourself, or something, to get you from one bit to the next. Read it out loud before you start. Long beautiful sentences often turn to soup in an induction.

Before you begin

Before you start:

Read this induction. Come all the way back again while you are reading it. Decide what it is you want to explore, what it is you want to leave alone, how much time you have. Maybe you just want to explore having more love or play or confidence or creativity or communion or whatever, you don't have to find a problem. Make sure you have enough time to come back out again and think about it.

Make sure you are safe. Don't do this if you are driving or near water or playing with machinery or around people you need to look after. Don't do this if you are intoxicated or in any state where you might be acutely confused or unable to look after yourself - in that case you need immediate support, not exploratory hypnosis. (But see the bit above about already being open, as this is not talking about deepening when unstable).

Practise First decide on how spacious, or how firmly inviting you wish to be. Let yourself know that you will need to close your eyes, and that you may need to come out a few times, as well as coming out at the end. If you are going to record the exercise, it may be a good idea to read the script first, if possible. Remind yourself that you can always stop the exercise by saying 'stop', or 'less', or 'quiet'. Remind yourself that you can always come out simply by opening your eyes, that you do not need to get everyone's agreement inside to finish.

It is wise, until you are fully confident about coming in and out, to practise in a context where you do not need to draw on your maximum efforts. Once you know how to change direction, you will not need to supervise all the time. Your response will get easier, and less effortful. A 'no' is a 'no' and silence does not give anyone the right to add to what is not there.

You will need to develop the next part of your induction, based on what you do get. This is the principle of utilizing what you do get, and it may change what you get. If you don't get anything, then you don't get anything! Remember that you need to lay out for yourself the instructions for safety and for coming out. You will learn more about the language you can use in Appendix B. And you will learn how to use them, once the induction is over, in Let the next response guide you .

Sober induction: 3–5 minutes

Guided Meditation: How to Listen These instructions are for use after you've read the chapter on Listening . It's best to practisise reading it slowly into a recorder, or read it aloud or if you're a pro even learn it and just say the words silently. Choose one of the three anchors to use, and read the instructions using that as 'the anchor' throughout. Also choose one of the opening phrases to use. At the end of each paragraph pause for a few moments. Don't read out loud the instructions for how to read it.

Let your eyes rest for a moment somewhere in the room.

As you do that, notice the surface that you are on, and how it feels to be in contact with it. As you do that, notice how even a sound, or a breath can bring your attention.

Remember that you have all the time in the world to do this.

Even if your attention is on a thought from the day, or even a thought about how you should be doing this, can you bring your attention back to your anchor even if there is a thought there?

In fact, notice one aspect of listening to the sound or being in contact or whatever you are doing to bring your attention which is interesting to you.

Remember that you can take as long to do this as you would give to a loved one if they were talking to you.

Now say to yourself (the opening phrase you've chosen) and notice how you receive that.

You can close your eyes or soften them or proceed with them open as you prefer. Notice how the listening opens up now, but perhaps you can still use the sound in the room in the back ground.

Now slowly count to yourself from 5 down to 1.

5 (notice your chosen anchor once more) 4 3 2 1

Bring to mind your chosen concern, or even just the wish to come into contact.

Now, what do you notice?

Take your time to notice what comes to you, whether it's sensations, words, images, feelings, urges to do something or even nothing at all.

Take your time to notice this, with or without words.

Working when you've already opened a state Before you try to deepen a state it's useful to contain it first.

Already open? Contain before you deepen

This is useful when you've already opened a state, through means other than doing a deliberate process - like taking loveyhuasca, doing a different style of meditation, being in a lucid dream, dealing with grief, listening to music, praying, engaging with erotic energy, exhaustion or even being overwhelmed by the beauty of something. When you've done that, then you want to stabilize the state before making it stronger.

Say to yourself 'The state is already open, now I just need to aim it, stabilize it and be kind to myself as I do.'

Look around you in the room, notice where you are and what date (or at least what day) it is. Feel your feet, hands and spine to ground yourself. Focus on the physical sensation of pressing your thumbs against your index fingers, feel the friction.

Say to yourself 'I will only allow myself to go as far as I can integrate. If there is more, it can wait. My body will be safe, my adult self will be present as my inner child deals with this.

Once you are oriented, then pick one of the following: 'Please show me the next thing I need to know, in a form (symbol, feeling, question, action) that I can integrate.'

Stay awake when your mind likes to escape

Staying awake when your mind wants to escape You can do this sitting up, with your eyes open, feeling your feet, and allowing your breathing to be natural.

Start by saying 'Today I am not going to escape from here into my mind, instead I will be more present here.'

Pick an object to look at, feel your spine as you do.

Now ask yourself 'Am I daydreaming in a way that is receiving guidance or helping me integrate emotional experiences, or am I escaping?'

Then say 'Please help me, if I am receiving guidance, to see what action I need to take, if I am escaping, please help me be present and show me what I am escaping.'

If whenever you stop, you escape into sleepiness and diffuse states, work on increasing your alertness instead of relaxing, keep your eyes open, work on doing something with your hands, doing it for a while, and then deliberately stopping it and noticing what comes afterwards without escaping into your mind.

For example say to yourself 'While you keep your eyes open, press your thumb and forefinger together and let go again a few times. Each time do it more clearly and in a more alert state. Now deliberately stop doing it and notice what happens in the first second after you do, do you feel an echo, or can you feel nothing?' Stay upright while you work at this level.

The two-hand induction

Where are YOUR hands? Put one of YOUR hands on YOUR heart. Put the other of YOUR hands on YOUR solar plexis.

The hand on YOUR heart is the Nurturer. The hand on YOUR solar plexis is the vulnerable child in YOU.

Breathe gently and affirm

The love is above and the child is below. And the adult is present.

I send love down to the child. And I receive signal from the child. Then I send more love down. And I listen to the signal again.

Sleep induction

This induction is different from the others, because in the others you need to get all the way back to your Adult to be able to write, do things, etc. In this case, the point is to go to sleep, so it is good for analysis to NOT be on duty and for revelation to wait.

To hear a hypnosis that will put you to sleep, check out Nimja's playlist here .

Optional fractionation: practice coming back

Ok, now I'd like you to open your eyes and come back. Do you want to stop the hypnosis? If not, close or soften your eyes and notice what's different as you go back into absorption. You can stop either way.

Deepening, if useful

Take yourself to your room in your heart, your garden or temple of inner peace, sit next to a fire with your Protector, float on a lake, sit in a chair where an adult waits for you, etc, etc, etc. Just pick one.

And see who wants to talk to you first.

Trance (optional):

Optional trance depth check

Give yourself permission to not have to do anything.

"If it is useful, my wise subconscious may cause one of my fingers to twitch, or pulse, or lift up, or get warm, or tingly, or whatever, to let me know that I am ready to meet with whomever wants to see me in my inner space." And of course you're not going to make it happen, or pretend it is happening, you're just going to wait in love.

It doesn't mean that anything will happen, but if something happens with one of your fingers, or you feel some other bodily change, none of it proves truth; at most, something may be listening.

A shortcut back into hypnosis

Once you've learned a useful induction and also the full return below, you can make up your own shortcut for getting back under hypnosis. My dad used to do a mudra (hand sign) by bringing two fingers together in an "okay" sign, and it would help him relax. He even did it while driving, but that's his experience, not a recommendation to enter trance at the wheel. So keep the cue you use for calming yourself while alert separate from the one for going into inward hypnosis!

Choose a Unique Word, Phrase or Movement You may want to add a gesture, but it's not necessary. When you are in a familiar and welcome hypnotic state that you like - not at the height of an emotional experience, and not in a child state or with a traumatic scene - start to pair that state with that word, phrase or gesture. You are giving that word, phrase or gesture a meaning that you choose.

When you are in a place and time where you have set aside time and it is appropriate and you want to deliberately start hypnosis with your short cut, then you can return to this familiar way of listening, from where you can change the direction of your experience or end the hypnosis.

Return fully. When at another appropriate time you want to deliberately start practicing hypnosis, use your short cut. Give it time. You can start to make your longer induction shorter as you find that the short cut works, but if it doesn't work, you can always use the familiar induction. There is no set number of times that you need to do this, or that you need to be instantaneously really deep into hypnosis or experience a particular sensation, it is completely up to you.

First, is it useful? Will it be there when you want it to be, not there when you don't want it to be? Can you change direction and return when you want to? It shouldn't become obedience to a narrator, notification, or overheard word. Going in faster doesn't determine what material you can handle.

Never train, test, or use hypnotic re-entry while driving or anything where you need to be actively paying attention even if it is open eyed and even if the words are conditional.

And if you don't want to any more, just stop doing it, remove it from any recordings you are using, any active apps, use an induction you are familiar with and state that you are finished using it whilst awake. If this doesn't stop the association straight away, and you are still getting unwanted affects or feeling disorientated, seek qualified help to sort it out. Until the next time you want to do it, you should not use the trigger.

Appendix B: NLP without turning yourself into a sales seminar

Appendix B - NLP (Neuro-Linguistic Programming)

You do not need to know this stuff to do it but if you want to freshen up on your skills in the art of working with imagery, body states, behavioural rehearsal, talking to yourself in effective sentences etc then it might be useful. Using the techniques can be an easy way to fall into the trap of thinking that NLP is a bag of tricks rather than something that needs to be done with love and truth and contact and consent.

The four NLP layers

The four levels of NLP are:

Sensory Level of NLP: working with the form of an inner experience (where do you see or hear it, how far away, how big, how bright, how loud, how do you hold your body, where is the pressure etc.)

Strategy level of NLP: practising a better response.

Language Level of NLP: pacing what is true; opening up people’s awareness; presuming you can do something safe; linking cause and effect; embedding invitations; asking de-hypnotic questions to break the effects of vague, absolutes, manipulative or grandiose language.

The Milton Model, minus the covert sales seminar

To do this we are going to use a model that’s called the Milton model. It’s all to do with sentence architecture. When we tell ourselves to ‘be better’, ‘relax now’, ‘stop feeling anxious’ or ‘trust me’ it doesn’t work, does it?

What we need to do is find a way of going around the part that wants to argue with us, so that we can actually get to where we want to get to.

So let’s start with something we know to be true, let’s take the pressure off, presume that we can only do a tiny bit and let’s invite one thing:

‘As my body begins to notice the sensation of the bed underneath it, it may be possible for it to begin to realise that it is not alone in carrying the burden of the day.’

We paced it; we opened up awareness; we validated the reason for the reaction; we presumed we could do it; we used a bridge word to make it easier and we invited one thing. We can then test this out with the body to see if it was possible.

Pattern 1: Pacing and leading — truth before suggestion

So how might we pace and lead in a way that works with anxiety?

It might go something like this: ‘It is completely true that the sensation of ________ (or the emotion of _____) is coming up for me. It makes complete sense that my system is trying to react and respond to that by wanting to do or think ________. Whilst that is completely true, there is another thing that is equally true, which is that my adult self is here, breathing in the room right now, and wanting to listen to what comes up for me next.’

Truth, Invite, Truth, Invite etc. is all you need to do.

Pattern 2: Awareness verbs

Open up awareness by using ‘awareness’ verbs e.g. notice, realise, recognise, sense, feel, wonder, imagine, picture, listen to, allow, discover, remember, consider etc.

Example: ‘Notice how you find out the answer.’

Pattern 3: Presuppositions

Presumption is a powerful thing, so please don’t use it except to presume that we will have the choice of when it will happen, that we will be able to do it, that we are safe, that we are loved and that our adult can lead us.

Pattern 4: Gentle cause-effect bridges

Be very careful here. Bridge words are words like ‘as, whilst, because, when, after, before, which means’ etc. These are words that link events. However, even if you say them in a lovely gentle voice it doesn’t mean that it’s true if it isn’t!

In general, the problem with the first example is that it’s too strong. It’s not very likely that just by breathing in and out that your trauma is going to go away! The second example is a lot better as it’s more true.

Pattern 5: Embedded invitations

ie. "And I can allow myself to experience..."

or, "As I sit here, I may begin to allow myself to become aware..."

Or, something similar that you might use when working with "inner child" type of parts.

You can use this, of course, but don't use ten of them one after the other! People will know that you've just come out of some weekend certification course and they won't feel so safe with you.

Pattern 6: Ethical double binds

Manipulative Double Bind Questions are like:

Ethical Double Bind Questions might be:

"Would you prefer to allow a feeling of warmth to come over you now, or would you prefer a feeling of space?"

Pattern 7: Conversational postulates

An example of a Conversational Postulate is:

"Can I allow the system to show me the next thing to do, without showing me all the details of wounding that are involved?"

Pattern 8: Tag questions

Similarly, you can use 'tag' questions, like "isn't it?" or "can't it?" or "doesn't it?" or others, but be aware that these can get pretty 'oily' pretty quickly, so don't overdo it.

"Your body knows how to relax, doesn't it?"

Pattern 9: Nominalizations

Nominalizations are words like, 'healing', 'safety', 'trust', 'integration', 'communion', 'clarity', 'rest', etc. These are a bit vague, and sometimes that can be useful, because it allows the subconscious to fill in the blank with something very specific for that person.

"I can allow myself some safety, in whatever way my body knows how."

Pattern 10: Meta Model questions — the de-hypnosis tool

To 'Milton Model' is to open things up. To 'Meta Model' is to say "What do yo mean by that?" In order to be ethical with people, you need to do both.

"What do you mean specifically? According to who? Compared to what? Always? Never? What specifically would happen if you did? How do you know that? What evidence could you have that would change your mind?"

When people are starting to get stiff in their bodies, 'Milton' it. When you feel like you're losing touch with the truth of what's going on, 'Meta' it.

Sensory, state, and strategy tools

Submodalities — editing the form, not denying the truth

If someone's fear, craving, fantasy, belief, memory, whatever, has sensory properties in your experience (it has a place in your visual field, or sounds a certain way, or is heavy, or moving, or inside / outside your body, or something like that), you can work with those properties. If there are no sensory properties that you can notice, don't try to create any -- just don't use this tool!

How is this represented for you? Can you allow yourself to move that image back a couple of feet? Can you soften the edges of that image? Can you turn the volume down on that voice in your head? Etc.

"And I can allow myself to know that I am not deleting the message, just turning down the volume so that I am able to be present enough to hear what it is."

And, always ask the guard if it's ok to do this.

"Is it ok to move that image back a couple of feet and turn the volume down a bit, so that I can be present enough to hear what you need me to hear?"

Anchoring — giving the body a doorway back

There are many ways to do this. Put your hand on your heart, touch two fingers together, use a breath, a word, a particular body posture, smell, song, whatever. Feel something that you have got to in reality that you want to be able to get to easily when you need to. Do your anchor thing and say to yourself that this is available to you. Do make sure you do it when you have clearly got it. To get yourself back into a good hypnosis state easily, dont go for a peak state but for a good hypnotic state. See the main induction for a quick way to get back into hypnosis. Do make sure this is different from both your alert and calm cue and your synchronicity wake up cue.

Using synchronicity as your own wake-up bell

Using synchronicity (The synchronicity wake up cue)

People often ask what the synchronicity means. Sometimes they get a great insight from it, but other times they get obsessed trying to work out patterns etc. I am using the noticing of the synchronicity to WAKE UP.

It is my cue to:

Whenever I notice it I use it as a cue for waking up from whatever state I am in, feeling my body, feeling the room I'm in, remembering that what I'm noticing is not proof for what I'm interpreting from the coincidences, widening my state so that I can see beyond what my current state is showing me. I then look for the truth of what is going on (What is really going on, what is just my interpretation? What needs to be warmed? What needs to be protected? What action needs to be taken?) and I go into the highest state I can get into where I can objectively and clearly see what is going on from that situation from the highest perspective I can get to, whilst remaining in my body, not leaving the facts of the situation and not leaving my regular human state. From that state I feel my feelings. I look for the truth of the situation. If I am in a negative state, I check if it is a message from my Inner Child, my Protector or if I just need to grieve. I check if it is a message from my physical body (if there is a problem with my body that needs to be taken care of) or if there is something that needs to be done about the situation. From that place I choose what to do. I choose at least one thing to do that is from a loving place. I allow myself to be in whatever state is real for me, which now includes objectivity, clarity, ease, peace, freedom, joy, gratitude, etc.

In other words: Stop-orient-go wider-reality check-listen-do at least one thing from a loving place.

This way I don't go into identification but I still hear the message of the state if it's negative.

Installing the synchronicity cue

How to install Synchronicity cues:

Mentally rehearse the following: Imagine that you have noticed a synchronicity that is obviously harmless.

Feel the "whoa" of stimulation that you just got from noticing it.

Use that stimulation to feel your feet, your body, your breathing, your room.

Reiterate to yourself that whenever you notice a synchronicity, it is just a bell that rings to wake you up, it is not proof for what you are interpreting from it.

Ask yourself: "What does my Nurturer think about this?", "What does my Protector think about this?", "What does my Leader think about this?"

Rehearse going back to a more grounded state and to a more wide view of the situation.

Rehearse yourself taking at least one action. Rehearse yourself waking up completely.

Mind the caveats! You must be the one authoring these. You must see them. You can always undo them. You must use them only to help you orient. They do not authorize you to make a decision. They are not proof for what your intuition is telling you. They do not stop you from hearing the message of your intuition if it is warning you about something. You can't use them to control other people.

This is very similar to implementation intention . I'm not aware of research into implementation intention for this specific thing, but the general mechanisms appear to work; a paper explaining how and why they work can be found here .

A downside of synchronicity cues is that they can lead to false positives. We do this on purpose when we rehearse what to do when we notice a synchronicity (we create an association in our head); however, when you are absorbed in something and/or when you are destabilized, you might think that you saw a synchronicity when in fact there wasn't any. Research has shown that people that score high on apophenia tests also score high for detecting patterns that were not really there, as well as scoring high on psychosis spectrum traits [1, 2] (this is not saying that noticing patterns is bad; in fact, it's not a pathology).

If you feel that synchronicity cues are making these things worse (e.g. you feel like you have to look for them all the time, you can't sleep, you feel anxious, you are sure that random things happen in your life in order to tell you something, you can't tell the difference between noticing something and interpreting what it might mean, etc.), you should deactivate synchronicity cues.

You can do that by not rehearsing them anymore and by saying to yourself (when you are fully awake) that you don't want to use synchronicity as a cue anymore (e.g. "From now on, I am no longer going to use noticing synchronicity as a cue for waking up."). Remove it from your list of cues, so that you won't rehearse it anymore.

Reframing — changing the meaning without lying

In the past I used to reframe by telling myself that whatever problem I had was actually a good thing. However, that is not honest. Now I reframe by asking myself:

Perceptual positions — self, other, witness, universal heart

Here is a rough outline of the NLP tools and techniques I use:

Perceptual Positions : 1) seeing from Self, 2) then seeing from Other, 3) then seeing from Witness, and 4) then seeing from Universal Heart. I do this to see the situation with more accuracy.

I will not use this to rationalize bad behavior, but only to break out of a prison of perception.

Future pacing — let the future test the insight

Future Pacing : 1) Once I have seen the situation more clearly, I will imagine future scenarios where my old behavior would have triggered, to test out if my new insight is working.

If these scenarios come up, I will choose new small behaviors using an Implementation Intention (If...then... statement)

The Swish, softened

Swish Variation : 2) I use an NLP technique called a "Swish Pattern", but I will allow my old pattern to be there, while also holding my new pattern in my awareness. I feel what comes up somatically, and compare the differences between the future scenarios of my old and new patterns.

Parts integration, without pretending the conflict is solved

Parts Integration : I use this technique to ask my conflicting parts what they want, what they are afraid of, what their need is, and see if I can find a 3rd option that satisfies both parts needs, without either part dominating my behavior.

What I will not use NLP for

Here is a list of things I do not do with NLP :

I do not deny people's legitimate signals.

I do not tell people to override their fear.

I do not use NLP for memory retrieval.

I do not use NLP to manipulate other people or convince myself of my intuition.

I do not remove legitimate signals or medical symptoms.

I do not use NLP on people who are panicked, destabilized, manic, having a "psychosis-like state", or are too high/dissociated to reality test.

I do not use NLP to make people feel like they are spiritually inferior to me if they disagree with me.

I do not use covert commands in my language.

I do not use NLP with people when there isn't enough time (I create urgency for them).

I do not use NLP on people without their consent (the idea that "your subconscious will let me know if you want me to do this" is NOT consent).

I do not use NLP on people in a suggestible state (in trance, tired, attracted to me, feeling shame or grief, or chemically altered).

Here is a rough outline of the entire NLP process (though I rarely do all of this) :

Running the whole NLP sequence

Induce/Contain the person (get their attention or stabilize them).

Ask for their permission.

Get a representation of their pattern (image, feeling, size, color, location, movement, etc.).

Find out what that part/pattern is protecting for them.

Change some aspect of their pattern (location, volume, space, posture, speed, etc.).

Put 3 good adults in with the person (Nurturer, Protector, and Leader).

Anchor the person's good state (heart, fingers, breath, posture, etc.).

Future pace a scenario for them where their old pattern would have triggered, and have them do a small new behavior (If...then... statement).

Have them check in with their body for changes and look for evidence to support their new interpretation of the situation.

Get the person out of the altered state (bring them back to the room and have them do something).

When this needs more support than a guide can provide

Remember, this is self-hypnosis, a relationship with yourself. If the situation calls for support, this guide isn't the right thing.

If you need help now: Get help now if you feel in imminent danger, very confused, or unable to keep yourself safe. Get help now if you have concerning physical symptoms (chest pain, fainting, etc.) You should seek professional help promptly if you have new or worsening suicidal thoughts, severe insomnia, new or worsening symptoms of mania or psychosis, or if dissociative symptoms are affecting your functioning. These are not problems that this guide will resolve in 4-12 weeks.

You probably don't need any more support than this: If you keep the practice shorter, make it warm, pick a small and tractable subject, make sure you come back out, and then see how it affects a specific target (anxiety, daydreaming, helping a relationship, facing a task you've been avoiding, helping you sleep, being less reactive emotionally, improving your intuitive accuracy, etc) for a week or two, and if you notice that your functioning is getting worse, or that you're getting more certain about unconfirmable memories, then reassess instead of pushing harder.

You should seek suitable ongoing help if: You are experiencing recurring panic attacks, compulsions, substance destabilization, major relationship instability, etc.

Methods to explore with a trained person present

If you want to deliberately do trauma-focused regression (going backwards in your memory or imagination to times when you were younger), or affect and somatic bridging (following associations from an emotional or somatic experience to find the origin of that experience, particularly if it was a traumatic experience you don't know about), or if you find that you're having substantial flashbacks or dissociative reactions, then you should do this with a trauma-informed clinician present. Make sure they're trained in the specific method you want to do. Ask any potential person what they would do and how they deal with uncertainty and unexpected reactions. Note that even if you work with a person, hypnosis is not a way of knowing what did or did not happen to you. (Both regression and affect/somatic bridging can also be used to find resources and do other things, of course.)

Note that having experienced trauma, crying, and even wanting to feel difficult feelings, are not necessarily signs that you need more support than working on your own. You get to pick how wide and narrow a range you want to work in, but be aware that different people need different ranges. Pay attention to how you respond and what support you have. Feeling like you are handling it isn't a substitute for having support.

Most clinical practice guidelines for the treatment of major trauma recommend one or more of trauma-specific variants of cognitive behavioral therapy (often referred to by specific names, such as cognitive processing therapy, prolonged exposure, etc.) or eye movement desensitization and reprocessing , and in some cases one or the other or both in addition to each other. These approaches in turn can be further supported by techniques such as self-hypnosis and inner child work. You need that bigger container when working with high-risk trauma.

Always keep in mind that your functioning in ordinary life is the feedback. If you find yourself more loving, more honest, more functional, more relational, more grounded, more precise, etc. than when you started this process, keep on keeping on gently. If you notice that your ordinary life is becoming less stable, don't try to go deeper. Go for more sleep, more eating, more grounding, more healthy boundaries with other people, more getting support from other people, etc.
HG14-rfix:
The inner child, the guards, and the three inner adults

Your inner child won’t trust you right away. It’s not going to be enough for you to meditate, say three nice sentences to the inner child and expect to have its trust. What’s going to help your inner child to trust you is you, the person you are right now, becoming reliable.

Here I’m going to talk about what you need to develop in yourself in order to be able to reparent your inner child. I’m going to talk about it in terms of three aspects: your Nurturer, your Protector and your Leader/Guru, but I don’t mean them as if there were really three people in you. It’s you that needs to develop these qualities.

Also, your inner child’s worth is not dependent on these qualities… It has its own worth, and its own qualities, like playing, being tender, not taking life too seriously, being creative and wondering at the world. Those belong in your relationship with it too, not just the wounds.

When the adult role is not available yet

The problem is, that some people do not have access to their adult functions at will. Instead, they may go blank, access an inherited inner critic, or feel like a child part who may be playing at being an adult. Telling them to just access their adult is like telling them to just be able to fly.

For that starting point, I use a provisional bridge I developed and call borrowed adulthood. Please note, it puts together familiar practices (witnessing, modeling, supported action, and handing over responsibility bit by bit), and I’m not claiming that the entirety of the steps has been validated as one treatment.

- Access a witnessing position, if necessary: notice what’s there without demanding warmth, wisdom or certainty. If you already know how to distinguish your internal positions, skip to the next step and access the adult position you need.

- Borrow an adult function. You may “borrow” this from a safe adult in your life, a mentor, an older sibling, a future version of yourself, a spiritual figure, a value, or even a written plan. Borrow only what you need right now – warmth, a boundary or direction.

- Put on the adult hat as an apprentice. Now, in this position, figure out what you would want to say or do – and then do at least a part of that.

- Return the adult hat, noticing what you borrowed and what you were able to do on your own (even if it’s only 5%).

This is a borrowed figure, so you’re still making the choice. The longer version of this exercise can be found in my Inner Child Self-Love Reparenting Guide .

You don’t have to have trustworthy people in your history. Use someone you remember when that helps, or just imagine a good adult whose intention is to take good care of you. See if you can imagine what they would say/do in your situation, with your history, limitations, options, etc. If you can’t imagine good, start with the least cruel response you can believe. Once you’ve found something good, try it, don’t keep doing the exercise.

It can be helpful to use borrowing when you’re in the adult position and not knowing what a decent adult would do, especially when the child doesn’t trust you and every response you can think of is retaliating, defending your goodness, collapsing or leaving. How would a decent adult hear that distrust? Borrow that one response. You may still feel young when you do it, it’s okay, feeling like an adult can come after you act like one.

Let the child speak without handing over the steering wheel

It’s possible to let the ‘younger’ parts of you express themselves without surrendering your adult judgement to an outside caretaker, and without literally reverting to a younger age. Instead, the aim is to access the positive aspects of ‘younger’ feeling states, such as a sense of wonder or playfulness, more direct sensory experiences, vulnerability, need, and a desire to carry fewer decisions.

"It is okay for a younger part of me to talk. But I understand that the adult in me is always going to be here, listening, evaluating, protecting me and stopping me if needed. I am not going to replace my adult judgement with any child state, guide, recording or person."

This way you get the benefits of being young; curiosity, spontaneity, play, sensation, the ability to state your needs, to feel easily etc without any of the negatives of being a child, like obeying, being helpless, being scolded, the lack of good judgement etc.

Love doesn’t have to wait for trust

Even if your inner child does not believe that you love him or her, you can still love him or her. Trust can question your promises, remember when you failed to protect him or her, and take its time.

You can say, out loud or in your head, “Okay. I believe that you don’t believe me, but I still love you. You don’t have to love me back. Please tell me what is not okay with you.”

Respond to complaints, which are likely to include something true. Showing that you love him or her can include some or all of the following: listening to him or her when he or she is angry without hitting back, owning up to what was not okay, working on being less likely to turn on him or her, and other ways of making it up to him or her. Other ways of showing that you love him or her include taking care of him or her by buying and cooking food, setting limits, taking him or her to doctor’s appointments, and doing what you say you will do. Just not hitting back is not enough; you also need to love your inner child.

Be aware of what you are teaching your other positions. You might be teaching your inner child that you are going to love him or her no matter what, but you might also be teaching him or her that he or she is responsible for believing your love, and that if he or she does not, it is his or her fault. The position that is making the vow to love the inner child no matter what, and the position that is blaming the inner child for not taking in the love, might be separate positions, or they might be one position, or you might be blending them. It might not be based on chronological age.

When you're placing your younger self on trial, how valuable is it for you to consider how valuable it might have been for your younger self at the time to be doing what they did, given what they knew at the time? How valuable is it for you to consider what options were available to them at the time, and how tolerable they were? How valuable is it for you to consider the consequences of their actions at the time? How valuable is it for you to consider that whilst their actions might have caused harm to you and others, punishing yourself now will not give them the capacity they needed at the time, and that it is more useful to work on what you can do now to deal with the harm that was caused?

WORKING WITH YOUR INNER CHILD:

The two-hand practice

There is a simple and easy body technique to connect with your inner child. Just place one hand in the center of your chest which is physically connecting you to your love and then place your other hand just below that which is your solar plexis and where your child can be.

Begin to send love from your heart down to your child and just notice what comes up for you. It doesn't matter if something comes up or not. If you feel resistance, just meet it with love. If you feel or see something, just meet that with love as well. This is a conversation with your child from your heart.

Remember, Love is on top, your child is on the bottom and you are there with them.

The Nurturer

THE NURTURER: As a Nurturer one of the most important things that you can do is to enjoy your inner child, to sit back and not feel like you have to move their feelings and to say to them that you are really glad that they are here in this moment. Children need to be enjoyed.

It’s okay that you’re feeling the way you are feeling.

I want you to know I’m here for you.

You don’t need to do anything right now.

It’s okay that you’re not too much. You can be small here.

You can be angry here.

You can be sad here.

The Protector

I’m going to be here for you.

The Protector:

Work with your Protector to set boundaries together. They might be small, like “I’m going to leave this conversation because it’s not safe,” or “I’m going to stop texting someone who destabilizes me.” They might be self-care related, like “I’m going to eat” or “I’m going to get sleep.” They might be trust-related, like “I’m going to keep this promise to myself” or “I’m not going to leave you alone to deal with these adult things.”

A lot of inner child work fails because we do all the fluffy stuff, but then we go text the person who destabilizes us or don’t eat or don’t do whatever thing we were meant to be doing. Trust comes from being able to handle adult things.

If you can’t bring up the warmth stuff yet, that’s okay, you can always do something to be protective of your inner child. Make sure they’re small enough that you can do them. If you can’t, figure out what’s getting in the way of doing them. Are you scared? Tired? Don’t know how? Is there a practical obstacle in your way? Did you set yourself up to do it successfully? Be careful not to define doing the thing successfully as “feeling good about it” or “being able to check it off a list.”

The Leader, Guide, or Guru

The Leader/Guide/Guru:

You can also work with your Leader. Call them whatever you want, Guide, Guru, Wise One, Sage, Inner Teacher, Director, Higher Adult, whatever.

Ask them for help with directing your life. Be careful not to ask for the kind of “tough it out, you don’t have needs, you just need discipline!” kind of direction, though. Ask them for help in directing you to do adult things in a way that takes your needs into account: asking for the help you need, expressing your preferences, letting a safe person see you in an imperfect way, finding ways to get your need for closeness met without punishing someone for their need for space, etc. etc.

Affirmations might be helpful here, too: “We’re not just here to feel good. We’re here to become whole. We’re here to belong to life, not only to people who approve of us. We’re here to serve truth/beauty/love/God/source/nature/the universe/dharma/the Tao/the benefit of all beings,” etc. etc.

Start with whatever adult function you can connect to. Even if you start with protection and can’t do the warmth stuff yet, make sure the direction you’re being led in is appropriate for your inner child’s growth (i.e. not depriving them of things they need, like play or support, etc.)

Working with protectors

Working with protectors:

Feel free to use parts language here, too, if it’s helpful. Often, we see a sensation or a distraction or an objection as something that needs to be explored, when in fact it might just be hunger, or reasonable skepticism about something, or a sentence that doesn’t fit. It’s good to notice it, though, and then to see what might be going on.

Most people assume when approaching their inner child that the first thing they’ll encounter is…their inner child.

But more often than not, what you actually experience is numbness, cynicism, anger, hunger, the sudden urge to check your phone, a sexual urge, mental planning, sleepiness, dissociation, or the simple thought that “this is stupid”. I wouldn’t call those failures. They’re often the protector, the guard at the door, showing up in its usual charming way.

One important voice to become aware of when approaching your inner child is your inherited parent. This is the voice of your parent(s) that you internalized as a child, based on how they treated you. This is not the same as your inner adult (Nurturer, Protector, Leader/Guru) that you will eventually build up. Often this inherited parent acts as a critic or warden, telling your inner child not to cry, not to be “needy”, not to embarrass them, not to be too independent, etc. So when you begin talking to your child in a new, loving way, this voice may jump in to say that what you’re doing is “fake”.

(“I notice you and what you are trying to do. I want to know more. Could I ask you what you are afraid would happen if you stopped protecting me by…..?)

If necessary take time and listen. (Perhaps they are afraid that you will lie to yourself again or pretend again or that it will be too painful or you will get spiritual bypass again or you will forgive someone who shouldn’t be forgiven yet or you will see what you want to see or that you will leave them hanging after the session or…..)

(Now talk to the protector. Tell them that it makes sense that they want to protect you and that they don’t have to stop protecting you, but that you want to know what could make them trust you 1% more that you can do that.)

Most of the time the protector wants you to do certain things, set boundaries, do whatever you are supposed to do, eat, not text someone, keep a promise, go to sleep, talk to the therapist, admit that you owe someone money, write something down, etc.

Protection that knows when to stop scanning

Do you want to “embody” your Protector? Then you could practice this:

1. orient self (look around, feel the support around you, etc.)

2. assess the situation (know what you know, what you don’t know and check out what you need to)

3. differentiate between actual/real danger, unknown, past or imagined dangers

4. set boundaries (start with one and make it relative to the danger; move, stop, delay, ask, leave, get support, etc.)

5. verify if it is safe enough

6. stand down and rest

This seems to me like a “mature” Protector. One that is not afraid to say that he doesn’t know, or one that can ask another human being, or one that can delay interpreting a situation or one that can use a no-trance method. I am learning to “do” discernment when I need to and stop scanning the room when it isn’t needed anymore.

Inner child reparenting

I see a lot of connection between reparenting therapy and self hypnosis. They fit well together. When you go into hypnosis the child might come to you. You might see that child in any form. It can be an image, a posture, a voice, a memory, an emotion, etc. It can be any age. It can be any vulnerable part of you. It doesn’t even have to be a “child”, if there is no child there, just work with a protector or whatever you find.

Don’t rush the repair

Just be with the child.

If you can, tell the child that you are there for them and that they don’t have to explain themselves, or be “healed” or impress you. Just tell you what they need to not be alone anymore.

It can be anything. What does the child need? warmth, to play, to be protected, to mourn, to be angry, food, rest, boundaries, better relationships, to stop fantasizing, to stop working their butt off, that you keep a promise to them for one day, etc. etc.

When “your voice” is everybody else’s voice

It can be difficult to connect with your inner child if your inner child didn’t have the opportunity to develop. This happens often when you grow up in a situation where you don’t have a private self, for example when your family, religion, or community ‘takes over’ very early in your life. Or you are pushed to achieve very early in life. The result is that you don’t know what you feel, what you want, what you believe, what you like and dislike until you have heard someone else’s opinion about it. If you are in that situation, it can be difficult to follow the advice to ‘love yourself’. You don’t even know who ‘yourself’ is! So you can do reparenting and finding yourself in parallel. For others, it is very easy to work with the inner child, they can feel it easily.

You are in this camp if:

You don’t know what you want, until you have heard what someone else wants.

Your opinion is very different when you are with different people

You agree with people at the moment but when you are by yourself you realize that you don’t agree with them

You take responsibility for the emotions of others, at the expense of yourself

When you try to love yourself, it feels more like a show

When you try to find out how your inner child feels, you feel that you are guessing instead of feeling

You can rebel, but you can’t choose

This happens because when you were a child, your attention went into avoiding pain, reading danger, meeting expectations and keeping the bond, so you didn’t have the opportunity to explore what you like, what you want to try out and who you are. This is not a claim about one specific brain system but a practical way to look at it.

Sometimes you need to distance yourself for a certain time from the people or group that you normally get your answers from. But not for too long, as then you defeat the purpose of this exercise! The distance helps quieter preferences surface, so you can tell your own signal from the social echo.

What is the difference between a human doer and a human being? If you don’t feel good enough as a human being, you will try to become good enough as a human doer by for example being beautiful, doing something well, being smart, having a certain status, being spiritual, etc. Those can all be real gifts. They become a bargain for belonging when failing in these areas feels like losing yourself.

So in order to find yourself, you can ask yourself:

What do I like when nobody is looking?

What do I believe when I don’t check with other people?

What do I want that is neither in rebellion nor in compliance with others?

Where am I buying my sense of belonging at the expense of betraying myself?

In what arena am I trying to buy my sense of belonging?

What can I try on that I don’t need to be good at?

With whom can I be myself?

What do I feel in my body and what do I make out of it?

Give your inner child the opportunity to do something that has no value on its own and that it doesn’t need to be good at for its resume. For example painting, dancing, gardening, learning a language, playing a sport, doing volunteer work, playing a musical instrument, etc. Because often your inner parent tells your inner child that it is supposed to be good at something as soon as it starts doing it. And that’s not good because your inner child will get humiliated that it isn’t good at it. The adult in you can answer, “We’re finding out whether we enjoy this, not proving our worth.” So try things out long enough until the humiliation is gone.

When you are a child, you will feel that you need to belong to a family in order to survive. That is why many people do things for their family, their religion, their romantic partner, their political tribe, their spiritual group, their institution or their online community that they otherwise wouldn’t do! Part of adulting is finding out where you sell yourself in order to belong, and then choosing your own ground, and learning that you can disappoint someone without disappearing. Because a large part of your subconscious mind, is made out of other people. This is why you are reading a self hypnosis guide!

Where am I betraying myself in order to belong?

What does it feel like to belong without betraying myself?

Where do I think I am following my own guidance, but I am in fact following my belonging program?

Where do I think I am doing things out of love, but I am actually doing it out of fear of not belonging?

Where do I think I am listening to my conscience, but I am actually listening to my conditioning?

Where do I think I am doing something out of devotion, but I am actually doing it out of compliance?

Where do I think I am free, but I am actually rebelling?

And then look what your body tells you. It is not always correct, but it is a good place to start.

Appendix D: Anxiety — body first

Remember that often the anxiety comes from a protector part, a part of yourself who is trying to help you, but who believes you are in danger, or may be shamed, or abandoned, or fail, or be exposed, or become sick, or rejected, or lose control, or suffer something else unbearable. Therefore, instead of an interrogation, start with yourself:

Always work with yourself by first taking care of your body, then your inner child, then some inner inquiry, and then some action:

Inner child love

Inner child love: Put a hand over your heart, and a hand on your solar plexis, and say lovingly, “Little one, you are not alone. You don’t have to fix this. I’m here now. The adult is listening.” Don’t just say the words, but say them in a way that you are talking to the inner child, who is frightened.

Reduced breathing / Buteyko-style breathing

Reduce your breathing. (NOTE: there are some good things to be said for slowing down the breathing, for some who overbreathe or are panicked, and this part is based on the Buteyko approach. But please don’t force yourself to hold your breath and suffer air hunger, which can make you more anxious for a short period. Proceed slowly.) Take small inhales through the nose, and quiet exhales, with pauses only if comfortable. Can you quiet your breathing? STOP if you feel dizzy, strained, or panicky, or experience any other medical concerns.

EFT tapping

EFT tapping: One of the easiest ways to do EFT is to say something like, “Even though I have this anxiety, I am willing to be kind to the part of me that is afraid,” while you tap gently on your body and stay with what you feel. There isn’t a ton of evidence for EFT, but there are some studies on anxiety. A 2025 systematic review found 7 randomized control trials for anxiety disorders, and noted that EFT was more effective than no intervention in a few studies. So use the evidence with caution, and know that there are first line therapies for anxiety.

Somatic Experiencing

Somatic experiencing: If you would like more information about somatic experiencing, or even a free intro session, please see my somatic guide . In somatic experiencing (SE), you are not thrusting into the trauma. You learn to track. So you might start by tracking, by discovering where the activation is, where a neutral place is, and then whether you can move your attention from one to the other, very slowly, like a snail.

Gendlin Focusing

Gendlin Focusing: Focusing is another approach where you work with your body. You might say to yourself, “What is the felt sense of this whole anxiety?” Don’t answer with your head; let your body come up with a vague sense of the whole anxiety. Then ask, “What would this felt sense like me to know?” Try a word or a phrase and see how well it fits the felt sense. But also see if what the word or phrase says is true of the situation. The word may feel ok, but say something that doesn’t fit the situation, or vice versa. Use the words and the body to mutually correct one another.

Body supports

Work with the body. Sometimes the mind is too activated for meditation to help, so you may need to work directly with the body to calm it down. Maybe get a massage, or massage a foot, your scalp, a temple, or the back of the neck, the top of a shoulder, etc. (Avoid massaging the front of the neck. Also avoid massaging injured or numb body parts, or bruised, inflamed, or recently surgically operated on areas, or varicose veins. Also stop if the massage makes the anxiety symptoms worse, or makes you feel bad in any way, such as painful, dizzy, tingly, etc.) There are many other somatic approaches you can try, like heat, pressure, a weighted blanket, darkness, your favorite calming music, a careful use of a massage gun, etc.

You may find that you settle down with some of these things: warmth, darkness, favorite music, massage, a weighted blanket, some breathwork, a favorite object, technology you use to relax, etc.

I have a page on my ZHoly3O product, which is ozonated charcoal, and I talk about this “holy water” as one of the things that can help you relax. (See the mention of Blushield on that page, too.) But neither one of those products are necessary. All you really need is to stabilize yourself, and then listen to the messages from your inner realm, reality test those messages (neither product proves they are true), and then take one grounded action.

A script you could use for anxiety is:

Anxiety script

Where am my body? What are my feet doing? How am I sitting in the chair? How am I breathing? How is my body in the room?

Little one, if you can hear me, I want you to know that I am here. Protector, thank you for alerting me. You don’t have to scream. I got your message.

Now if there is something we need to do, show me what the first thing is that we should do, right now. And if there is nothing we need to do, help my body stand down, and know that I am not going to abandon you, but I am also not going to worship you. I am going to listen to you, reality test what you are saying, and then take some action.

Appendix E: Is the daydream helping or replacing your life?

Sometimes daydreaming is something that your subconscious mind is doing to help you. It is simulating an idea or event to help you digest grief or teach you something. The very act of daydreaming may be helping you to access your creativity or allowing your subconscious to show you a potential future. Sometimes your subconcious will show you things that you may be afraid of. Sometimes it will show you what you want.

Other times daydreaming may be taking you away from your life in a detrimental way. It may be that you are escaping reality and are addicted to fantasies rather than the real life. You may be dissociating or obsessing about romantic partners or escaping from being an adult.

How do you know which it is? Simply ask yourself if the daydreaming is taking you closer to life, with more clarity, love and ability to take action or if it is taking you away from life, in a repetitive and craving way.

If it is helping you then simply ask yourself what the guidance is and how you can use it.

If it is taking you away from life then change your body position by sitting upright, open your eyes, feel your feet and ask your subconscious to help you. Simply say to yourself, “Dear subconscious thank you for showing me images. If what you are showing me is helpful then please also show me the helpfulness in it. If what you are showing me is a way of avoiding dealing with life then please show me in a gentle but structured way how to deal with life as it is right now.”

Then ask yourself what it is that you need to do in “real” life that you are avoiding by daydreaming.

You may need to send a text message or stop sending text messages. You may need to clean up your room, eat, sleep, deal with grief, create, apologize, leave, tell the truth, make a plan, get help, get back to a task that you were supposed to be doing, stop chasing love that is not available to you etc.

Come all the way back

Come out of the session by reversing the entry method; if you floated, come back down by the same method; land with your chosen weight. If you shrunk, come back to your normal size. If you meet your younger self or parts, make sure that you acknowledge that you are now whole, this is your body, and you are using your adult judgement. If you traveled, then come back the same way you left. Make sure that you are only bringing back what you had intended to bring back.

You may wish to say, “I am bringing back only that which I choose to bring back at this time. All that is not needed at this time will remain safely stored away until such time as I am ready. I am now coming back to this place and to my body and to normal day to day living. All instructions to go deeper or stay in this session are now over, except for the conscious intention (or cue) I chose for the future, and that doesn’t keep today’s state going. I’m myself again, in my body, with my adult judgment.”

Count yourself out: 1. Coming back into your body and your chosen weight. 2. Coming back to your normal breathing pattern. 3. Coming back to awareness of your surroundings and of your location. 4. Moving your fingers and your toes and your shoulders and your eyes. 5. Opening your eyes, feeling present, normal and clear. Your session is now over.

It is a good idea to say to yourself what day it is or what the date is, look to your left and to your right, look at something near and something far away, move about a bit before you stand up, stand up only when you’re steady, and make sure that you are actually oriented and alert (repeating the count isn’t proof that you’re all the way back). Take note of anything that came up during your session and what you may or may not need to do as a result, and then just go about doing something normal.

In the event that a recording that you are listening to stops unexpectedly, simply say to yourself “the recording has stopped and the session is over” and then use the above method to come out by opening your eyes, saying where you are, saying what day it is, pushing down with your feet or your hands, moving about, looking around and then using the 5 step method. Don’t sit there waiting for the voice to come back and release you.

Note: If you are using a recording to go to sleep, then it is all right to let the recording put you to sleep or have you in a quiet resting state. However, if it’s a recording for waking practice, then it should not leave you in any state that is not conducive to normal functioning, such as leaving you in a role, with lowered judgement, impaired movement capabilities, blank, with an undefined reset word, or invited to stay altered indefinitely.
